newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWB Report - Rain good for Australia sorghum.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWB Report - Rain good for Australia sorghum.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said the summer storm rainfall pattern across much of the eastern states grain belt has producers optimistic about the new season.
In the north, sorghum harvest has been halted temporarily in the western parts of Queensland but has been insufficient, at this stage to cause any damage to the downs crop.
Most focus is currently on sorghum, the size of the crop and the potential, if any for exports.

At the end of the week, sorghum was priced around $115 a tonne on the Queensland Downs which would put it at $160 to $162 in Sydney and Newcastle and $130 a tonne delivered Brisbane. "The price and the depressed state of the store cattle market is encouraging some restocking of feed lots and mat out pressure on stocks of sorghum" the AWB said.
Export parity this week is around $126 to $127 a tonne.
AWB confirmed in its weekly grain market report that it had sold 400,000 tonnes of ASW wheat to Egypt for March delivery this week.
The USDA report released mid-week contained few surprises, boosting Australia's wheat production to 23.1 million tonnes and expected exports to 13.5 million tonnes.
As a reflection of the logistic problems that Canada is experiencing, it dropped that country estimated exports to 13 million tonne.
Initially, that sort of news is supportive of the market but in the longer term Canada's 12.3 million tonne carry over (almost twice what it came into the season with) will have an impact on prices.

The corn figures show a five million tonne increase in China's production compared to last season and Argentina continues to have a good year with a 3.5 million tonne increase over last season's production.

At 576 million tonnes estimated world corn production is 60.2 million tonnes up on last year and the stocks to use ration has moved out from a very tight 11.6 percent to a still extremely tight figure of 14 percent.
The AWB estimate of the national wheat crop remains at 23 million tonnes.
